title: CDL Pre-Trip Inspection & Air Brake Test

jurisdictions._note: The app ships to two schools in two states. Each student is assigned a jurisdiction once; all checklist wording and any threshold overrides come from here. Overrides are deliberately empty until confirmed against each state's current examiner sheet — see docs/06_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md Q1.

tenancy._note: Built school-only but tenant-ready: every run, progress and leaderboard row carries an org_id from day one so multi-school can be switched on later without a data migration. See BUILD_SPEC.md.

standards._note: Thresholds are configuration, never hardcoded in components. The static leak limit was disputed between the booklet (4 psi/min Class A) and the air-brake handout (3 released / 4 applied); RESOLVED 2026-09-08 by Alexandre in favour of the handout, for both FL and MA. The booklet's figure is retained below as leak_limit_booklet_psi_per_min for reference only and is NOT used for grading.

grading.credit_rule: You MUST name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain what you are inspecting each safety-critical item for. If you do not, you get no credit.
grading.auto_fail_behaviour: Missing any auto_fail item ends the run immediately with a FAIL and a written explanation of what was missed.

items.label: Seat Belt
items.script: My seat belt is tight and secure at the top and the bottom, no cuts, no fraying, and it latches and releases properly.
items.coach_tip: Physically tug the belt while you say it. Examiners want to see the check, not just hear it.

items.label: Air Valves — Set
items.script: Both air valves are activated in the up position — the yellow parking brake valve and the red trailer air supply valve are pulled out.
items.coach_tip: Yellow = tractor parking brake. Red = trailer air supply. Up/out means APPLIED.

items.label: Gear Shift
items.script: My gear shift lever is in neutral.

items.label: Safe Start
items.script: I will safely start the engine: brakes are set, shifter is in neutral. Key to the on position — I check that my ABS and DEF lights come on and go off — then I start the motor.

concepts.label: ABS and DEF lights come on and go off

items.coach_tip: If the ABS light stays on, that is a defect — say so out loud.
common_errors: Forgetting to call out the ABS/DEF lamp check

sections.title: In-Cab Air Brake Check
sections.note: Marked on the official checklist as automatic failure if not performed correctly.

items.label: Air Compressor — Governor Cut-Out
items.script: With the engine on I fast-idle the truck up to between 120 and 140 psi, at which point the governor cut-out should occur. I'll hear the air release after the cut-out. My needle stopped at ___ psi — cut-out works.
items.coach_tip: Say the number you actually see. The grader wants a real reading, not a range.

items.label: Static Air Leak Test
items.script: Engine off, key on, air valves pushed in. I depress and hold the brake pedal, wait for the gauge to stabilize, and start my timer. In one minute I cannot lose more than {{leak_limit_applied_psi_per_min}} psi. Starting at ___ psi — it's been one minute and I lost only ___ psi. I did not lose more than {{leak_limit_applied_psi_per_min}} psi.
items.coach_tip: You must actually let 60 seconds run. Rushing the timer is a fail.

items.label: Low Air Warning — Light and Buzzer
items.script: Engine off, key on, valves pushed in. I fan the brake pedal down. The low air warning light and buzzer must come on at or above 55 psi. It came on at ___ psi — my low air warning works.

items.label: Spring Brakes — Pop-Out
items.script: I continue fanning the brakes down. Between 45 and 20 psi both brake valves must pop out on their own. I'm looking at the valves, not the gauge — I do not pull the valves. They popped out at ___ psi — my spring brakes work.
items.coach_tip: Tell the examiner as EACH valve pops. If only one pops, keep fanning until the second pops.
common_errors: Pulling the valves by hand — automatic fail
Watching the gauge instead of the valves

items.label: Air Pressure Build-Up Rate
items.script: Parking brakes on, shifter in neutral, I safely start the engine and hold 1500 rpm. First my low air warning must shut off at or above 55 psi. Then I time from 85 to 100 psi at idle — it must take 45 seconds or less. It took ___ seconds.

concepts.label: Warning shuts off at or above 55

items.coach_tip: Optional in some states, required in others. Check your examiner's sheet.

items.label: Tractor Parking Brake Check
items.script: I release the trailer brake — push the red valve in — put the truck in gear and try to move it lightly. The truck does not move, which means my tractor parking brakes hold.

concepts.label: Puts it in gear and tries to move
States the truck did not move

items.label: Trailer Brake Check
items.script: I release the tractor parking brake — push the yellow valve in — and leave the red valve out. I put the truck in gear and try to move it lightly. The truck does not move, which means my trailer brakes hold and the trailer stayed connected.

concepts.label: Puts it in gear and tries to move
States the truck did not move

items.label: Service Brake Check
items.script: I release both parking and trailer brakes — both valves in. I put the truck in gear and move forward between 5 and 10 mph, then apply the service brake. The truck stops straight: no pulling to the left or right, no unusual feel to the pedal, no delay in stopping, no chatter, no unusual sounds or smells.

concepts.label: Does not pull left or right
No unusual feel, delay, chatter or noise

items.label: Dashboard Light Indicators
items.script: With my lights on I check my dashboard indicators: high beams show a blue light, my right and left turn signals show flashing green arrows, and my four-way flashers show both green arrows flashing together.

items.label: Fire Extinguisher
items.script: My fire extinguisher is tight and secure, fully charged in the green, up to date, and the pin is present and secure.

items.label: Reflective Triangles
items.script: I have three reflective warning triangles, tight and secure, no damage, and clean.

items.label: Spare Fuses
items.script: I carry one box of extra fuses and relays — at least six spare fuses.
items.coach_tip: Not required if the vehicle has no fuses — say that instead if it's all breakers.

sections.title: Windshield, Mirrors, Wipers, Heater & Horns
sections.checklist_category: windshield & traffic monitoring devices / wipers & washers / heater & defroster / horn(s)

items.label: Windshield
items.script: My windshield is tight and secure, no cracks, no illegal stickers, clean, and nothing is blocking my view.

items.label: Mirrors
items.script: My mirrors are adjusted to me, tight and secure, no cracks, not broken, clean, no illegal stickers, and nothing is blocking my view.

items.label: Windshield Wipers
items.script: My wipers are properly mounted with no missing bolts, not broken, blades have no splits or cuts, and they sit even with the windshield.

items.label: Washer Fluid
items.script: Washer fluid is present, and the wipers and washer are working properly.

items.label: Heater / Defroster
items.script: I demonstrate that both my heater and my defroster are operational.

items.label: Horns
items.script: I ensure both horns are operational — my city horn and my highway air horn.

sections.title: Lights Operations Check
sections.strategy: Group similar lights together (headlights + high beams; turn signals + 4-way flashers; brake lights + tail lights). Four sides of the truck, four sides of the trailer — follow the flow and you won't miss any.

sections.title: Front of Vehicle / Engine Area
sections.checklist_category: lenses / fluid levels / fluid & air leaks / steering systems

items.label: Truck Leveled
items.script: My truck is leveled and there are no leaks underneath — no oil, no grease, no coolant.

items.label: Clearance, Flasher & Signal Lights
items.script: My clearance, flasher and signal lights are tight and secure, no cracks, and the proper color.

items.label: Headlights — High and Low Beam
items.script: My headlights, high beam and low beam, are tight and secure, no cracks, clean, and the proper color.

items.label: Coolant
items.script: I verify the coolant is at the proper level through the sight glass or dipstick. The reservoir is properly mounted and not cracked, and the hoses have no splits or cuts and are securely mounted at both ends.

concepts.label: Hoses no splits or cuts, secure both ends

items.label: Engine Oil
items.script: I indicate where my dipstick is located and that the oil is at the proper level.

items.label: Power Steering Fluid
items.script: I verify the power steering fluid is at the proper level through the sight glass or dipstick. The reservoir is securely mounted and not cracked, and the hoses have no splits or cuts and are securely mounted at both ends.

concepts.label: Hoses no splits or cuts, secure both ends

items.label: Fluid & Air Leaks
items.script: Standing in front of the truck, I ensure there are no leaks underneath the engine compartment. I verify all the hoses in the engine compartment — no cuts, no bubbles, no leaks.

concepts.label: All hoses — no cuts, bubbles or leaks

items.label: Steering Gear Box
items.script: My steering gear box is properly mounted to the frame, not cracked, not leaking, all hardware is present, and the hose has no leaks and is properly mounted at both ends.

items.label: Pitman Arm
items.script: My pitman arm is not cracked and securely mounted, all hardware is present, and the castle nuts and cotter pins are in place.

concepts.label: Castle nuts and cotter pins in place

items.label: Drag Link
items.script: My drag link is properly mounted at both ends, all hardware is present, and the rubber bushings are not split or cut and are properly greased.

concepts.label: Rubber bushings not split or cut

items.label: Upper & Lower Control Arms
items.script: My upper and lower control arms are not broken and securely mounted, all hardware present.

items.label: Tie Rod
items.script: My tie rod is not broken and securely mounted, all hardware present, castle nuts and cotter pins in place.

sections.title: Steering Axle
sections.checklist_category: tires / rims / lug nuts / springs & mounts & shocks / brake lines & hoses / brake contaminates

items.label: Front Tire
items.script: My steer tire is evenly worn with tread depth no less than four thirty-seconds. No cuts, no bulges, no bubbles, no air leaks, no recaps on the steer axle, and no flat spots. Properly inflated at around 100 psi.

concepts.label: No recaps on the steer axle

items.coach_tip: Steer tires need 4/32". Every other tire on the vehicle needs 2/32". Never call a recap legal on the steer axle.

items.label: Rims
items.script: My rims are tight and secure, no cracks, no bends, not broken, no illegal welds, and no illegal holes.

items.label: Lug Nuts
items.script: My lug nuts are tight and secure, all present, no cracks, and no rust streaks — if I see rust they might be loose and they need to be tightened. No bolt holes elongated.
items.coach_tip: Explaining WHY rust matters — 'rust means it may be loose' — is what earns the credit.

items.label: Spring Mounts
items.script: My spring mounts and hardware are not cracked or broken and are properly mounted to the frame.

items.label: Leaf Springs
items.script: My leaf springs are not shifted or scissoring, no illegal welds, and they're properly mounted to the spring hangers.

items.label: U-Bolts
items.script: My U-bolts are not cracked or broken, no loose parts, and no missing bolts.

items.label: Shock Absorber
items.script: My shock absorber is not bent or broken and is mounted securely, no visible leaks, and the rubber bushings are not worn.

items.label: Air Brake System Hose
items.script: My air brake hose is tight and secure with fittings at both ends, no cracks, no air leaks, not worn, and no dry rot.

items.label: Air Chamber
items.script: My air chamber is properly mounted, tight and secure, no cracks, not broken, no air leaks, and the clamps are tight and not missing.

items.label: Brake Drums, Shoes & Linings
items.script: My brake drum is not cracked and my shoes and linings are not worn thinner than a quarter inch. There are no contaminants — no oil, no grease, no debris between the brake drum and the brake shoes.
items.coach_tip: 'Brake contaminates' is its own line on the official checklist — say the words 'no oil, no grease, no debris' explicitly.

sections.title: Side of Vehicle
sections.checklist_category: lenses & reflectors / traffic monitoring devices / battery / fuel & DEF tanks / frame

items.label: Turn Signal Light & Reflectors
items.script: My turn signal light is tight and secure, no cracks, clean, proper amber color, and it works as a signal light and as an emergency light. My reflectors are amber at the front and red at the back.

items.label: Mirrors (Traffic Monitoring Devices)
items.script: My mirrors are tight and secure to the door, no cracks, not broken, clean, and no illegal stickers blocking my view.

items.label: Fuel Tank
items.script: My fuel tank is tight and secure, no cracks, not bent, no leaks. The cap is present, tight and secure. The straps are secure and not cracked.

items.label: DEF Tank
items.script: My DEF tank is tight and secure, no cracks, not bent, no leaks. The cap is present, tight and secure, no cracks or leaks.

items.label: Battery
items.script: My battery box and cover are secured, no cracks, no broken welds, and the battery connectors are secured. The cables and wires are not exposed, corroded, ripped or torn.

concepts.label: Cables not exposed, corroded or torn

items.label: Frame
items.script: My frame has no cracks, is not bent, twisted or broken, no illegal welding, and no rust through.

sections.title: Combination Vehicles Only
sections.checklist_category: air & electric lines & connectors / fifth wheel / kingpin & apron & gap / locking & safety devices

items.label: Electrical Line
items.script: My electrical line — the green cable — is flexible and doesn't touch the frame, catwalk, tractor or trailer. No exposed wires and no illegal taping. It's tight and secure to my tractor with the seven pins and to my trailer's electrical box with the seven pins. The pins are not bent or broken, no debris, and all seven are present.

concepts.label: No exposed wires or illegal tape
All seven pins present, not bent

items.label: Air Lines — Service & Emergency
items.script: My service line is the blue hose and my emergency line is the red hose. They don't touch the tractor, trailer or catwalk, they're flexible, no cuts, no bubbles, no leaks. They're tight and secure to my tractor with the fittings and to my trailer with the glad hands, and the glad hand rubber seals are not worn.

concepts.label: Glad hands secure, seals not worn

items.label: Fifth Wheel Skid Plate
items.script: My fifth wheel skid plate is tight and secure to the platform, no cracks, not broken, no illegal welding, and properly greased. There is no space between the skid plate and the apron.

concepts.label: No gap between skid plate and apron

items.coach_tip: 'No gap' is the safety-critical part — a visible gap means the trailer can separate.

items.label: King Pin & Apron
items.script: My king pin is securely mounted, not bent or cracked, no illegal welding, and fully greased. My apron is securely mounted to the trailer, not cracked or broken, and has no illegal holes or welds.

items.label: Locking Jaws
items.script: My locking jaw is securely mounted, no cracks, no illegal welds, fully greased, and it's in the locked position all the way around the king pin.

concepts.label: Closed all the way around the king pin

items.label: Mounting Pins, Release Handle & Pivot Pins
items.script: My mounting pins are present, fully engaged and in the locked position. My release handle is not broken and is in the locked position all the way in. My pivot pins are present, not cracked or broken.

items.label: Landing Gear
items.script: My landing gear is fully raised, properly mounted, not broken, no illegal welding. The crank handle is present, not broken, secured in its holder, and it's operational.

items.label: Trailer Clearance Lights
items.script: My trailer clearance lights are tight and secure, clean, not cracked, proper amber color on the front and red on the back.

items.label: DOT Reflective Tape
items.script: My DOT tape is present, properly fastened, not dirty, and covers at least fifty percent of the side of my trailer. Proper red and clear color.

items.label: Lenses & Reflectors
items.script: My lenses and reflectors are not cracked, broken or loose, they're clean and the proper color. They function as turn signals, emergency lights, brake lights, markers and reflectors.

items.label: Clearance Lights
items.script: My clearance lights are tight, secure, no cracks, proper color, clean and working.

items.label: Turn, Brake, Clearance & Flasher Lights
items.script: My turn signals, brake lights, clearance lights and flasher lights are tight, secure, no cracks, proper color and working.

items.label: Railroad Crossing Procedure
items.script: At two hundred feet I turn my flashers on and check for traffic. I move forward between fifteen and fifty feet from the tracks. I stop, lower my window, look and listen for a train. I don't see or hear a train — it's safe. I have space on the other side to clear the tracks completely. I stay to my right. I move forward without changing gears. Once the trailer passes the tracks I turn my flashers off, check my traffic and accelerate.

concepts.label: Has room to clear the far side
No gear change on the tracks

items.coach_tip: Never shift on the tracks. Never stop on the tracks. Both are instant fails.
common_errors: Shifting gears while on the tracks
Stopping with any part of the rig on the tracks
Forgetting to turn the flashers back off

items.label: Emergency Stop Procedure
items.script: I will pull to the side of the road, put my brake valves up, put my truck in neutral, turn on my four-way flashers, and place my three reflective triangles. Then I check for traffic before I get back in and accelerate.
items.coach_tip: Triangle placement: 10 ft behind, 100 ft behind, and 100 ft ahead on a two-lane road.
